questions.q: What is the real difference between sys.dm_exec_sessions and sys.dm_exec_requests?
options: Sessions only shows Azure SQL Database; requests only shows on-prem SQL Server
Sessions is one row per connection whether or not it's doing anything; requests is one row per request actively executing right now
They return identical information in a different column order
Requests shows historical data; sessions shows only the current second
questions.explain: A session can sit idle for hours; a request only appears in sys.dm_exec_requests while a batch is actively running.

questions.q: What does filtering sys.dm_exec_sessions to is_user_process = 1 accomplish?
options: Removes all Billing department connections
Drops SQL Server's own internal system sessions, leaving only real client connections
Shows only sessions connected through SSMS specifically
Shows only sessions that are currently blocked
questions.explain: is_user_process = 1 excludes SQL Server's internal system sessions so you only see real application/user connections.

questions.q: What does a non-zero blocking_session_id on a row in sys.dm_exec_requests tell you?
options: That request is using the most CPU time of all current requests
That request has already finished executing
That request belongs to the Scheduling application specifically
That request is waiting on another session, not genuinely slow on its own
questions.explain: blocking_session_id being non-zero means the request's wait is caused by another session holding a lock — a different problem from the query itself being slow.

questions.q: What column is the fastest way to tell which department's traffic a session belongs to?
options: program_name
wait_type
session_id
cpu_time
questions.explain: program_name identifies which application (Billing vs. Scheduling) made the connection, without needing to know every login name.

questions.q: Why query sys.dm_exec_requests specifically during the reported mid-morning window?
options: It is the only DMV available on Azure SQL Database
Running it at any other time would return an error
It only returns data during that specific time of day by design
It captures the actual long-running requests happening during the window both departments complained about
questions.explain: Running the query during the reported window captures the real requests that are actively executing when the slowness is happening.
